# Source manifest and data provenance

Generated by `scripts/build_manifest.py` from the files actually present. Machine-readable copy: `data/source_manifest.json` (includes every file's SHA-256).

## 1. Provenance in one paragraph

**All data in this project is synthetic and generated by this repository's code.** No external or public dataset was downloaded, copied, scraped or transformed; nothing was retrieved from the web; no access controls were involved; no personal, confidential or customer data was used. Because no external data is used, there is no source URL, dataset version, retrieval date, licence, attribution, transformation list or discarded-field list to record (the fields the problem statement asks for would all read "not applicable").

| Item | Statement |
|---|---|
| External datasets | none |
| Fictional content | operator and engineer names (Faker, seeded; entirely fictional), employee ids `EMP-nnnnn` (synthetic), plant names (invented labels) |
| Real-world labels | plant cities, countries and time zones are real place names used only as labels; machine types and interlock types are generic industrial terms |
| Public reference material | concepts only, for schema and rule inspiration: alarm-management practice (alarm floods, chattering / nuisance alarms, acknowledgement deadlines - e.g. ISA-18.2 / IEC 62682 terminology) and machine-safeguarding vocabulary (interlocks, guard locks, e-stops, light curtains). No text, tables or data were copied. All thresholds are this project's own configurable defaults (`docs/business_rules.md`), not normative values of any standard |
| Personal data | none; names are random and fictional, any resemblance to real people is coincidental |

## 2. How the data is produced

* Entry point `python data_generator/generate.py --scale full` (generator version **1.0.0**, fixed seed **20261022**; `--seed` overrides).
* Window: 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31 UTC (30 days). Full scale: 4 plants, 60 machines, 200 alarm definitions, 50,000 baseline alarm events. Starter scale: 2 plants, 8 machines, 40 definitions, 2,000 events, 7 days. Same code, different presets.
* Each generation stage has its own random stream derived from the seed, so stages do not disturb each other. Outcomes are derived by the rules in `backend/app/business_rules`, not assigned independently.
* Valid baseline first, then five labelled anomalies appended to a copy (`data_generator/anomaly_injector.py`); labels are written to separate ground-truth files and the database schema `gt`.
* Reproducibility evidence: `docs/reproducibility_report.md`.

| Tables | How produced | Derived columns |
|---|---|---|
| plant, machine, safety_zone, machine_safety_zone, interlock | seeded draws from fixed template lists (cities, industries, machine types, interlock plans per machine type) | none |
| alarm_severity_policy | copied from the documented rule defaults (`RulesConfig`) | priority_rank, deadlines |
| alarm_definition | templates by trigger type x machine type x interlock type, numbered variants | none |
| operator_shift, shift_machine_assignment | three 8-hour shifts per plant-local day, two operators per shift, machines split by slot | shift window (UTC), assignments |
| machine_state_event, interlock_state_event | per-machine seeded state machine with an allowed-transition graph; unsafe excursions at documented probabilities | interlock_status_summary, safety_assessment, unsafe_rule_code (rules R-U/R-S/R-I), shift_id |
| alarm_event | state-driven alarms, planted floods and nuisance clusters, background alarms filling the target count exactly | severity (AL-1), ack_deadline_at (AL-2), lifecycle_status, machine_state_event_id, shift_id |
| acknowledgement | delay and missing-acknowledgement outcome from workload, shift and repeat rules | ack_delay_seconds, ack_status (AL-4) |
| incident, incident_alarm_link, incident_status_event | created by rule IN-1 from unsafe episodes; timeline from per-severity ranges truncated at the cut-off | severity (IN-2), status and milestone timestamps from the history |
| corrective_action, corrective_action_status_event | chains per incident with verification outcome by action type (CA-4) | status and timestamps from the history |
| injected anomalies (appended rows) | five labelled scenarios appended to a copy of the baseline | derived columns by the same rules |
| ground truth (separate files / schema gt) | labels written by the generator, never read by detectors or KPIs | n/a |
